B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP price is stated. Era's Basic plan is free and lists 100 MCP tool calls per day; paid plans list 250, 1,000, and 10,000 daily calls, with an add-on for extra MCP calls.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Basic: free. Organize: $6.99/month billed yearly at $83.88. Automate: $17.49/month billed yearly at $209.88. Operate: $69.99/month per seat billed yearly at $839.88. Listed prices are in USD.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Plan-based access and quotas. Pricing page also lists add-ons: extra MCP calls $2.79/month billed yearly; other account, rules/category, and sync add-ons are separately priced. Paid tiers may offer a trial or paid introductory offer.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Tools vary by plan, approved OAuth scopes, connected accounts, and MCP client. Billing changes require mcp:billing-write, which docs say is outside the default scopes. Some tools are marked plan-required. Money movement is described as private beta and off by default for every API key; transfers require approval.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Era controls plan entitlements, server-side scope checks, and tool availability; the user approves OAuth scopes or configures an API key; the client controls whether it surfaces safety labels and asks for confirmation.

The resource metadata names https://mcp.era.app as authorization server, supports bearer tokens in headers, and lists scopes. The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants, S256 PKCE, public token clients (token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ["none"]), and Dynamic Client Registration. Revocation endpoint auth method is none. Token lifetime not disclosed. The supplied OIDC configuration URL returned 404.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official tool list labels tools read-only, write-capable, and sometimes destructive or extra-consent/plan-required. MCP tool annotation fields themselves are not published. 2. Docs describe client confirmation for destructive tools; transfers require user approval before running, and billing has preview/confirm tools plus mcp:billing-write. Destructive-tool confirmation is phrased as a client expectation, not a server guarantee. 3. Input-host OAuth metadata lists scopes; product docs say availability also depends on plan, scopes, connected accounts, and client. Docs describe per-assistant OAuth approval and revocation; consent-approved access expires within an hour after revocation. API key expiry is user-selected; token lifetime and redirect-URI approval rules not found. 4. No read-only endpoint or URL/header tool filters documented. Basic plan is described as read-only; plan and scope access varies. Money movement private beta. 5. Docs say agents do not receive bank credentials; bank auth is handled by regulated aggregators. Privacy page describes account data, retention, and deletion, but tool-level field masking/boundaries not specified. 6. Pricing sets daily MCP call quotas by plan (100/250/1,000/10,000) and an extra-call add-on; no MCP per-call price or result cap documented. Docs mention rate-limit failures without values. 7. Schemas and server-side validation/correction behavior not published. 8. Era says agent reads and writes are logged in an activity log; privacy policy says residual copies may remain in backups, security, audit, and system logs. 9. Tools include referral enrollment, campaign switching, links, stats, and dashboard access; these can support referral activity. No feedback/rating tool found in official list. 10. No server-delivered skills documented; behavioral guidance appears in tool descriptions/docs and client prompts. 11. Knowledge tools persist user financial facts/questions across connected agents; saved memory changes later context. 12. No subserver/proxy architecture documented. 13. No raw API, SQL, or script escape-hatch tool appears in the official tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Memory should come from explicit approval, not inference.
Rules keep changing future data, so agents should preview and ask before applying them.
Uncertain transfer matches should be confirmed with you.
Disconnecting an institution is destructive and should require clear confirmation.
Review the current plan, compare options, preview exact cost changes, and only then confirm or open checkout.
Context moves money between your own accounts only after your explicit approval on every transfer. It can't pay bills, place trades, file taxes, or act outside the tools listed here.
Destructive tools should be surfaced clearly by the client and confirmed by you.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: A flat categorized tool list is documented. The product also shares user memory across clients, but no tool hierarchy or subserver is described.

The supplied endpoint host is mcp.era.app, whereas the official tool list and server card identify context.era.app. The 89 listed actions are therefore best-available official product evidence, not independently verified as the supplied host's tools. Claude's connector directory lists 27 tools; Composio lists 51; Agent Discoverability lists 50. These are incomplete subsets; no extra catalogue-only names were added. MCP.so reports no tool list available. Tool schemas/parameters are not published in the official list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs recommend starting with read-only questions, previewing and asking before applying automation rules, and having clients surface and confirm destructive tools. The destructive-action confirmation is explicitly phrased as a client responsibility: "Destructive tools should be surfaced clearly by the client and confirmed by you."
F_documentation.governance_promises: Era states: "Agents do not receive bank credentials." It says bank credentials are not stored, OAuth scopes limit access, tool availability depends on plan and scopes, billing changes require separate consent, and agent activity is logged. Privacy policy says account data is retained while the account is active and as reasonably necessary, with deletion/de-identification after request subject to legal exceptions and residual copies in routine backups and logs.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Era describes access as scoped and revocable, memory as private to the user and shared only across that user's connected agents, and account data as not sold. It says users can inspect agent activity and revoke access.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata confirms an authorization server, scopes, registration, code/refresh grants, and PKCE. The docs describe approval and revocation but do not establish tool-specific enforcement details for the supplied host. Approval for transfers and separate billing scope are documented as controls; destructive-tool confirmation is client-side guidance. Logging, credential protection, and retention claims are product/privacy statements, not independently verified from public server code.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint is https://mcp.era.app/mcp and has its own OAuth metadata, while Era's official help page and server card document https://context.era.app and https://context.era.app/mcp. The official 89-tool list is for the documented product endpoint; equivalence of the two hosts is not established.

The supplied OAuth metadata includes mcp:billing-write, while Era's docs say billing changes require that separate scope and that it is not included in default scopes. The metadata lists supported scopes, not which are granted by default.
Claude's connector directory exposes 27 tools and Composio lists 51, compared with the official help page's 89 tools. These catalogues appear to show subsets; the official list takes precedence.
observations_for_research: The docs distinguish server-side permissioning from client-mediated safety: scopes and plan affect availability, while confirmation of destructive actions is recommended as a client behavior.
Financial memory is a cross-agent product feature: remembered facts and preferences are available to other connected agents, and tools can remember or forget facts.
Billing has a separate OAuth scope and a documented preview/confirm sequence; transfer actions are described as private beta with per-transfer approval.
The OAuth metadata for the supplied host offers a distinct resource identity from the currently documented context.era.app endpoint, making endpoint identity a material evidence limitation.
